result.summary: Exposes block storage management directly in the libbitcoinkernel C API by introducing `btck_BlockManagerOptions` and `btck_BlockManager`. Moves block storage configuration and read functions (`btck_block_read`, `btck_block_spent_outputs_read`) from the chainstate manager to the block manager. Callers create the block manager independently and pass it into `btck_chainstate_manager_create`, which retains a shared reference.
result.problem: In libbitcoinkernel, block storage is created internally by and tightly coupled to the chainstate manager. External callers cannot configure, retain, or prune block storage independently, preventing kernel users from working with pruned block directories.
evidence: PR description: 'Pruning (#35627) needs block storage that the caller can configure, keep and prune directly.'
Commit bfb52b50f5: 'Check the BlockManager directly, keeping one source of truth before the kernel can enable pruning.'
result.scope_notes: This PR is stacked on top of PR #36739 and shares refactoring commits that decouple BlockManager from ChainstateManager internally.
result.card: Exposes BlockManager management directly in the libbitcoinkernel C API rather than instantiating it inside ChainstateManager. Callers can configure and own block storage independently through new btck_BlockManager and btck_BlockManagerOptions handles, passing the block manager into chainstate creation. This decouples storage lifecycles and unblocks issue #35627 to allow kernel callers to work with pruned block directories. The PR is stacked on #36739.

risk.why: Alters lifecycle management and initialization ordering of core validation storage structures, where reference counting or destruction ordering bugs could cause memory corruption or crashes.
